statements.says: Administrative courts are the court of general jurisdiction in administrative disputes, except disputes assigned to other courts.

Administrative courts decide at first instance, with appeal, all cases where the State, a wilaya, a commune, an administrative public institution, a national public body or a national professional organisation is a party.

Administrative courts also hear actions to annul, interpret or review the legality of decisions of the wilaya, State local services, communes, regional professional organisations and local administrative public institutions.
Administrative courts hear full-jurisdiction actions.
Administrative courts hear cases given to them by special texts.
By exception to articles 800 and 801, road offences stay with the ordinary courts.
By exception to articles 800 and 801, liability actions for damage caused by a vehicle of the State, a wilaya, a commune or an administrative public institution stay with the ordinary courts.
The specialised commercial court hears the disputes listed below.
Intellectual property disputes go to the specialised commercial court.
Commercial company disputes (partners, dissolution, liquidation) go to the specialised commercial court.
Judicial settlement and bankruptcy go to the specialised commercial court.
Disputes of banks and financial institutions with traders go to the specialised commercial court.
Maritime and air transport disputes and insurance disputes linked to commercial activity go to the specialised commercial court.
International trade disputes go to the specialised commercial court.
The territorial jurisdiction rules of the code apply to the specialised commercial court.
Conciliation precedes registration of the claim, on a party's request to the court president, who appoints a judge within 5 days; conciliation lasts at most 3 months.
After failed conciliation the claim is filed by petition with the record of non-conciliation attached, on pain of inadmissibility in form.
The specialised commercial court rules by a judgment appealable to the judicial council.
The president of the specialised commercial court holds the powers of an ordinary court president in commercial disputes, and a section head may order urgent interim measures.
A creditor of a sum of money that is due, payable, fixed in amount and proved in writing may, instead of the ordinary claim, petition the president of the court of the debtor's domicile.
The petition, in two copies, states the parties, the legal person's details, a short account of the debt, with all proofs attached.
The president rules by order within 5 days of filing: if the debt is proved he orders payment, otherwise he rejects.
A rejection order cannot be appealed, but the creditor may bring a normal claim.
The order is formally served with a summons to pay within 15 days, stating the 15-day right to object on pain of nullity.
Objection is made by urgent procedure before the issuing judge and suspends enforcement.
Without objection in time the order becomes final and the enforcement formula is granted.
An order not presented for the enforcement formula within one year lapses.

sections.matter: Disputes listed in 536 مكرر (intellectual property, commercial companies, bankruptcy, banks, maritime/air/insurance, international trade)

territory.rule: The ordinary territorial jurisdiction rules of the code apply to the specialised commercial court.
territory.when: Claim before the specialised commercial court

territory.rule: Payment-order petition goes to the president of the court in whose area the debtor is domiciled.

exits.when: The State, a wilaya, a commune, an administrative public institution, a national public body or a national professional organisation is a party, or the case is an annulment, interpretation, legality or full-jurisdiction action or one assigned by special text
Road offences, or liability actions for damage from a vehicle of the State, a wilaya, a commune or an administrative public institution
Dispute is one of intellectual property, commercial companies, bankruptcy/settlement, bank with trader, maritime/air transport/commercial insurance, or international trade
Money debt due, payable, fixed in amount and proved in writing, and the creditor chooses a petition instead of a claim

openPoints.question: Is the payment order optional or compulsory for a creditor who meets the 306 conditions?
readings: Optional: 306 says the creditor 'may' (يجوز) petition, 'contrary to the rules on filing claims'.
Compulsory in practice: no text given says an ordinary claim is barred.

openPoints.question: Does the 15-day objection period of 308 run from service on the debtor, and is the 15-day period to pay the same period?
readings: Both are one 15-day period from formal service.
Two separate periods that merely coincide in length.

openPoints.question: When does the 3-month conciliation period of 536 مكرر 4 start?
readings: From the appointment order of the judge.

openPoints.question: Which administrative-court limb applies when the claimed party is a public body but the dispute is private-law in nature?
readings: 800¶2 applies by the organic criterion (any party listed), so the administrative court hears it.
Only if not assigned to another court (800¶1), so some such disputes stay ordinary.

openPoints.question: Can the commercial-dispute list in 536 مكرر be read as covering every dispute between traders?
readings: The words 'لا سيما' in the company item show only that item is illustrative; the list otherwise appears closed.

missingTexts.why: General jurisdiction of the tribunal and its sections is not given; needed to place ordinary civil, commercial and other sections.
General territorial jurisdiction rules referred to by 536 مكرر 1 are not given.
Referred to by 536 مكرر 7 on the public prosecution; not given.
No text on the criminal judge's jurisdiction (civil action attached to a criminal case) is given, so that exit cannot be derived.
Rules on administrative-court territorial jurisdiction and exceptions are not given.
How the periods in 307-309 and 536 مكرر 4 are counted (first or last day, non-working day) is not given.
Cases assigned to administrative courts by special texts (801¶8) are not given.
